User authorization and preferences persist across turns. Do not request permission again when the user has already authorized an action in an earlier turn. tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.6-sol`: Older generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

# Cooperative membrane-receptor thermodynamics

A membrane patch is represented by a finite lattice of interacting receptors. Each receptor has an inactive state $ s=-1 $ and an active state $ s=+1 $. The coupling map is heterogeneous: positive couplings favor agreement between neighboring receptors, while negative couplings favor opposite states. There is no single-site bias or applied ligand field. This is an idealized equilibrium model of receptor cooperativity, with dimensionless parameters already expressed in units of thermal energy.

Compute the partition function and the full joint activity distribution of the six designated probe receptors. The joint distribution is needed to quantify responses to combinations of locally imposed active or inactive states. Retain the finite lattice and both periodic boundaries in the calculation.

## Inputs and equilibrium model

The inputs are in `/root/data`:

- `model.json` gives `width`, `height`, and six probe records in the ordered list `probes`. Each record has an identifier and integer coordinates `x,y`.
- `couplings.csv` has columns `x,y,direction,K`. A row with direction `E` connects $ (x,y) $ to $ ((x+1)\bmod W,y) $; direction `N` connects $ (x,y) $ to $ (x,(y+1)\bmod H) $. Coordinates start at zero. Every undirected nearest-neighbor edge appears exactly once, including the wraparound edges. The listed decimal values of `K` define the model; there is no additional temperature factor.

For a complete receptor-state assignment $ s $, define

$$ B(s)=\sum_{e=\{u,v\}} K_e s_u s_v, \qquad Z=\sum_{s\in\{-1,+1\}^{WH}} \exp(B(s)). $$

Its equilibrium probability is $ \exp(B(s))/Z $. The six-character probe pattern uses the order of the `probes` list, with `0` meaning inactive and `1` meaning active. Its joint probability is the sum of equilibrium probabilities over all assignments with that probe pattern; all other receptors remain free to fluctuate. This is an unconditional joint distribution, not a product of individual activation probabilities. Use the natural logarithm for $ \log Z $.

## Deliverables

Write these two regular UTF-8 CSV files:

1. `/root/results/joint.csv`, with the literal header `pattern,probability` and exactly 64 data rows, one for every six-character binary pattern. Preserve leading zeros. Rows may be in any order.
2. `/root/results/thermodynamics.csv`, with the literal header `quantity,value` and exactly one data row whose quantity is `log_partition` and whose value is $ \log Z $.

Every numeric field must be a finite ASCII base-10 number, without surrounding whitespace; a decimal point and a base-10 exponent are allowed. Each file must be at most 1 MiB. Include no extra columns or blank rows. LF and CRLF line endings are accepted.

Each joint probability must be within absolute error $ 10^{-7} $ of the finite-model value, and `log_partition` within absolute error $ 10^{-7} $. Probabilities must lie in $ [0,1] $ and sum to one within $ 2\times10^{-7} $. Global state-inversion symmetry requires complementary probe patterns to have equal probabilities within $ 2\times10^{-7} $, and each probe's active-state marginal to equal $ 1/2 $ within $ 2\times10^{-7} $. Retain enough digits in the CSV files to meet these requirements.

Python 3, NumPy, and SciPy are available. You may use any computational method and install additional tools. No particular code structure or algorithm is required.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Finite zero-field torus Ising partition function and probe joint law.

The high-temperature even-subgraph polynomial is evaluated with four signed
Pfaffians of a terminal graph.  For an even set of probe insertions, XORing a
path with every even subgraph changes the tanh weight on each path edge from
t to 1/t; the path's original weight is then restored as a prefactor.
"""

import csv
import heapq
import itertools
import json
import math
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from pfapack import pfaffian


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Edge:
    x: int
    y: int
    direction: str
    K: float
    u: int
    v: int
    terminal_u: int
    terminal_v: int

    @property
    def t(self):
        return math.tanh(self.K)


class TorusIsing:
    sectors = ((1, 1), (-1, 1), (1, -1), (-1, -1))
    sector_coefficients = (0.5, 0.5, 0.5, -0.5)

    def __init__(self, width, height, edge_rows, probe_vertices):
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.n = width * height
        self.probes = probe_vertices
        assert width % 2 == 1 and height % 2 == 1
        assert width >= 3 and height >= 3
        assert len(set(probe_vertices)) == len(probe_vertices)
        self.edges = []
        self.adjacency = [[] for _ in range(self.n)]
        seen = set()
        for row in edge_rows:
            x, y, d, K = int(row['x']), int(row['y']), row['direction'], float(row['K'])
            assert 0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height and d in ('E', 'N')
            assert (x, y, d) not in seen
            seen.add((x, y, d))
            u = y * width + x
            if d == 'E':
                v = y * width + (x + 1) % width
                tu, tv = 4 * u, 4 * v + 2
            else:
                v = ((y + 1) % height) * width + x
                tu, tv = 4 * u + 1, 4 * v + 3
            edge = Edge(x, y, d, K, u, v, tu, tv)
            assert edge.t != 0
            eid = len(self.edges)
            self.edges.append(edge)
            self.adjacency[u].append((v, eid))
            self.adjacency[v].append((u, eid))
        assert len(self.edges) == 2 * self.n
        assert len(seen) == 2 * self.n
        assert all(len(adj) == 4 for adj in self.adjacency)

        # Local order is E, N, W, S.  This 4-by-4 skew block has Pfaffian 1.
        local = np.array(((0, 1, -1, 1),
                          (-1, 0, 1, -1),
                          (1, -1, 0, 1),
                          (-1, 1, -1, 0)), dtype=float)
        self.local_matrix = np.zeros((4 * self.n, 4 * self.n), dtype=float, order='F')
        for v in range(self.n):
            self.local_matrix[4*v:4*v+4, 4*v:4*v+4] = local

        self.base_matrices = [self.matrix_for_sector(tx, ty)
                              for tx, ty in self.sectors]
        self.baseline_pfaffians = self.four_pfaffians(self.base_matrices)
        self.even_polynomial = self.combine_pfaffians(self.baseline_pfaffians)
        assert self.even_polynomial > 0
        self.log_partition = (
            self.n * math.log(2) +
            math.fsum(math.log(math.cosh(edge.K)) for edge in self.edges) +
            math.log(self.even_polynomial)
        )
        self.pair_paths = {}
        for i, j in itertools.combinations(range(len(self.probes)), 2):
            self.pair_paths[i, j] = self.shortest_path(self.probes[i], self.probes[j])

    def matrix_for_sector(self, tx, ty):
        A = self.local_matrix.copy(order='F')
        for edge in self.edges:
            twist = (tx if edge.direction == 'E' and edge.x == self.width - 1 else
                     ty if edge.direction == 'N' and edge.y == self.height - 1 else 1)
            value = twist * edge.t
            A[edge.terminal_u, edge.terminal_v] = value
            A[edge.terminal_v, edge.terminal_u] = -value
        return A

    @staticmethod
    def four_pfaffians(matrices):
        return [float(pfaffian.pfaffian(A.copy(order='F'), method='P', overwrite_a=True))
                for A in matrices]

    @classmethod
    def combine_pfaffians(cls, values):
        return math.fsum(c * v for c, v in zip(cls.sector_coefficients, values))

    def shortest_path(self, source, target):
        dist = [math.inf] * self.n
        prev = [None] * self.n
        dist[source] = 0.0
        heap = [(0.0, source)]
        while heap:
            cost, u = heapq.heappop(heap)
            if cost != dist[u]:
                continue
            if u == target:
                break
            for v, eid in self.adjacency[u]:
                new_cost = cost - math.log(abs(self.edges[eid].t))
                if new_cost < dist[v]:
                    dist[v] = new_cost
                    prev[v] = (u, eid)
                    heapq.heappush(heap, (new_cost, v))
        assert math.isfinite(dist[target])
        result = set()
        v = target
        while v != source:
            u, eid = prev[v]
            result.add(eid)
            v = u
        return frozenset(result)

    def path_for_mask(self, mask):
        if mask == 0:
            return frozenset()
        assert mask.bit_count() % 2 == 0

        def candidate_paths(remaining):
            if remaining == 0:
                yield frozenset()
                return
            first = (remaining & -remaining).bit_length() - 1
            rest = remaining ^ (1 << first)
            for j in range(first + 1, len(self.probes)):
                if rest & (1 << j):
                    pair = self.pair_paths[first, j]
                    for residual in candidate_paths(rest ^ (1 << j)):
                        yield pair.symmetric_difference(residual)

        paths = list(candidate_paths(mask))
        return min(paths, key=lambda path: math.fsum(-math.log(abs(self.edges[e].t))
                                                     for e in path))

    def modified_even_polynomial(self, path):
        matrices = []
        for sector_index, (tx, ty) in enumerate(self.sectors):
            A = self.base_matrices[sector_index].copy(order='F')
            for eid in path:
                edge = self.edges[eid]
                original = A[edge.terminal_u, edge.terminal_v]
                new_value = original / (edge.t * edge.t)
                A[edge.terminal_u, edge.terminal_v] = new_value
                A[edge.terminal_v, edge.terminal_u] = -new_value
            matrices.append(A)
        pf = self.four_pfaffians(matrices)
        return self.combine_pfaffians(pf), pf

    def moment_for_path(self, path):
        prefactor = math.prod(self.edges[eid].t for eid in path)
        modified, pf = self.modified_even_polynomial(path)
        moment = prefactor * modified / self.even_polynomial
        return moment, pf

    def moments(self):
        n_probe = len(self.probes)
        values = {0: 1.0}
        for mask in range(1, 1 << n_probe):
            if mask.bit_count() % 2:
                values[mask] = 0.0
                continue
            path = self.path_for_mask(mask)
            values[mask], _ = self.moment_for_path(path)
            if abs(values[mask]) > 1 + 1e-8:
                raise ArithmeticError(f'impossible moment {mask}: {values[mask]}')
        return values

    def joint(self, moments):
        n_probe = len(self.probes)
        output = {}
        for bits in itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=n_probe):
            spins = tuple(2*b - 1 for b in bits)
            terms = []
            for mask, moment in moments.items():
                factor = math.prod(spins[i] for i in range(n_probe) if mask & (1 << i))
                terms.append(moment * factor)
            pattern = ''.join(map(str, bits))
            output[pattern] = math.fsum(terms) / (1 << n_probe)
        return output


def small_self_test():
    width, height = 3, 3
    rng = np.random.default_rng(62057)
    rows = [{'x': x, 'y': y, 'direction': d, 'K': float(rng.uniform(-0.4, 0.7))}
            for y in range(height) for x in range(width) for d in ('E', 'N')]
    probes = (0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8)
    model = TorusIsing(width, height, rows, probes)
    actual = model.joint(model.moments())
    brute = {''.join(map(str, bits)): 0.0
             for bits in itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=6)}
    Z = 0.0
    for spins in itertools.product((-1, 1), repeat=width * height):
        weight = math.exp(math.fsum(edge.K * spins[edge.u] * spins[edge.v]
                                    for edge in model.edges))
        pattern = ''.join(str((spins[v] + 1) // 2) for v in probes)
        brute[pattern] += weight
        Z += weight
    assert abs(model.log_partition - math.log(Z)) < 1e-12
    assert max(abs(actual[p] - brute[p] / Z) for p in actual) < 1e-12
    print('Small-torus exhaustive test passed', flush=True)


def main():
    small_self_test()
    model_data = json.loads(Path('/root/data/model.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    width, height = model_data['width'], model_data['height']
    probes = tuple(record['y'] * width + record['x'] for record in model_data['probes'])
    with Path('/root/data/couplings.csv').open(newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        edge_rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
    model = TorusIsing(width, height, edge_rows, probes)
    print('Baseline Pfaffians:', model.baseline_pfaffians, flush=True)
    print('log Z:', model.log_partition, flush=True)
    moments = model.moments()
    joint = model.joint(moments)
    print('Moments:', moments, flush=True)
    print('Joint range, sum:', min(joint.values()), max(joint.values()),
          math.fsum(joint.values()), flush=True)
    assert min(joint.values()) >= -1e-12
    assert max(joint.values()) <= 1 + 1e-12
    assert abs(math.fsum(joint.values()) - 1) < 1e-12
    assert max(abs(joint[p] - joint[''.join('1' if b == '0' else '0' for b in p)])
               for p in joint) < 1e-12

    # A change by one contractible plaquette leaves the path's odd boundary
    # unchanged, so the resulting moments must agree.
    plaquette = frozenset(next(i for i, e in enumerate(model.edges)
                                 if (e.x, e.y, e.direction) == key)
                           for key in ((0, 0, 'E'), (1, 0, 'N'),
                                       (0, 1, 'E'), (0, 0, 'N')))
    for mask in (0b000011, 0b110101):
        original = model.path_for_mask(mask)
        alternate = original.symmetric_difference(plaquette)
        check, _ = model.moment_for_path(alternate)
        assert abs(check - moments[mask]) < 2e-10, (mask, check, moments[mask])
    print('Path independence checks passed', flush=True)

    output_dir = Path('/root/results')
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with (output_dir / 'joint.csv').open('w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f, lineterminator='\n')
        writer.writerow(('pattern', 'probability'))
        for pattern in sorted(joint):
            writer.writerow((pattern, format(joint[pattern], '.17g')))
    with (output_dir / 'thermodynamics.csv').open('w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f, lineterminator='\n')
        writer.writerow(('quantity', 'value'))
        writer.writerow(('log_partition', format(model.log_partition, '.17g')))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
